analyst_view.overall: Early view: Roma play this four days after visiting PSG in the Champions League, but at home Gasperini's side have been dominant, as in the 3-0 against Sassuolo before the break. Svilar and Dybala should be back by then if their recoveries go to plan, while Pellegrini's return will take longer. Monza have lost four in a row and will be under even more pressure if they lose to Fiorentina; Juric was sent off at the end of the Atalanta game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, mostly Roma's. That fits: Roma's home games average 3.6 goals, and Monza's away games 4.0. Coming four days after PSG could take some edge off Roma, but Monza concede almost 2.7 a game away.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners. I lean higher: Roma win over seven corners a game at home and won 12 against Sassuolo. Gasperini's wing-backs keep putting crosses in, which produces corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: Roma's home games and Monza's away games have each averaged about 3.8 cards. Juric's sending-off against Atalanta shows how tense things are at Monza, so a high count is possible, but the averages point a little below the number.

shots.text: The site expects 28.5 shots. I lean higher because Roma's home games have averaged almost 34 shots, with Roma taking about 23 a game, including 28 against Sassuolo. Monza also shoot reasonably often, with Varela the main threat.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target, close to Roma's home average of about 11 and Monza's away figure of about ten. I stay with the number.
